gist: More homeowners are conducting their own heat loss calculations before buying heat pumps.
Tradespeople often overestimate required heat pump sizes, leading to inefficient, uncomfortable heating systems.
Experts disagree on whether homeowner self-surveys help or if installer practices must improve.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: More homeowners are using apps like Cool Calc to calculate home heat loss before purchasing a heat pump. A Purdue University study revealed tradespeople frequently overestimate design heat loads by a factor of two or more.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Inaccurate estimates result in underpowered heat pumps or oversized systems that cycle rapidly, causing temperature fluctuations and using excessive energy. Additionally, homeowners face high survey costs and potential misinformation from AI tools.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Cool Calc plans to integrate with AI chatbots to improve advice. Some firms suggest preliminary self-surveys will shorten professional visits, while other experts insist installer practices must improve rather than relying on homeowners.

gist: Three central banks published findings from Project Meridian FX APAC on foreign exchange settlement.
The trial showed synchronisation can link foreign exchange settlement across diverse central bank systems.
Findings will help inform the Bank of England's planned live synchronisation interface for 2028.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Bank of England, Monetary Authority of Singapore, and Bank of Thailand published findings from Project Meridian FX APAC. Delivered with partner Partior, the project tested synchronised payment-versus-payment foreign exchange settlement and multilateral net settlement across central bank test environments with different technologies.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Synchronisation coordinates central bank money movements across different technologies, reducing cross-border settlement risk and improving liquidity efficiency without requiring identical operating models.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Bank of England plans to launch a live synchronisation interface in 2028, with future work potentially extending to extra currencies, jurisdictions, and participants.

sections.text: The findings have sparked a debate regarding a potential knitwear gender gap.
